subjectOf.text: JPM Coin's closed structure, restricting the token to existing J.P. Morgan clients, is an anachronism, because closed ecosystems are unsustainable in emerging decentralized commerce.
subjectOf.abstract: The close structure of the JPM coin, e.g. JPM makes it only available to existing clients, appears to be an anachronism.95 Closed ecosystems are unsustainable in the emerging decentralized commerce.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Stable Cryptocurrencies (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3396522
scope_conditions: applies to permissioned stable cryptocurrencies limited to a single institution's clients

subjectOf.text: The cryptocurrency market structure is fundamentally convoluted because each project requires its own volatile token, which is equivalent to forcing grocery shoppers to buy a different currency for every store and every product.
subjectOf.abstract: The market structure of cryptocurrencies from its inception to 2019 can be compared to mandating customers who wish to purchase groceries to purchase a different currency for each store they visit and for each product chosen in such store.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Stable Cryptocurrencies (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3396522
scope_conditions: describes the market from inception through 2019

subjectOf.text: The interoperability deficit in cryptocurrency markets is partly intrinsic to blockchain technology itself, because the consensus mechanism that allows block propagation on one chain in some ways negates interoperability with other chains and their consensus.
subjectOf.abstract: The lack of interoperability can in part be traced back to blockchain technology itself. The consensus created to allow block propagation in some ways negates interoperability with other chains and their consensus.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Stable Cryptocurrencies (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3396522

subjectOf.text: The lack of interoperability is a very serious threat to the survivability of cryptocurrency projects, as the crypto winter of 2018 and 2019 demonstrated when thousands of competing, non interoperable projects failed.
subjectOf.abstract: The lack of interoperability is a very serious threat of survivability of cryptocurrency projects.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Stable Cryptocurrencies (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3396522

subjectOf.text: Currency stability should be used as the consumer facing proxy for interoperability, because teaching the public to value stability is easier than educating it about the blockchain technology that produces technical interoperability.
subjectOf.abstract: Rather than using technological solutions and educating the public on the blockchain technology that helps create interoperability, currency stability, and the public's recognition of the desirability of currency stability, serves as a proxy for interoperability.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Vadhindran K. Rao, Stable Cryptocurrencies (2019). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3396522

subjectOf.text: DeFi's decentralization remains theoretical in one important respect: as of the early 2020s DeFi is still largely relegated to one dominant platform, with 87 percent of all publicly funded DeFi projects built on Ethereum.
subjectOf.abstract: At the beginning of the 2020s, DeFi is still largely relegated to the use of one dominant platform. 87% of all publicly funded DeFi projects have been built on Ethereum.
subjectOf.citation: Kaal, Digital Asset Market Evolution (2020). SSRN: https://papers.ssrn.com/sol3/papers.cfm?abstract_id=3606663
scope_conditions: publicly funded DeFi projects
beginning of the 2020s

subjectOf.text: Instead of building compatible technologies in the service of interoperability, most crypto projects compete with each other, contradicting the open source culture the space needs if it has any hope of thriving.

subjectOf.text: Interoperability, meaning the API economy, is most efficiently achieved in the long run on decentralized platforms, because negotiations on a level playing field are fairer, resolve quicker, and encourage more business.
subjectOf.abstract: Interoperability, the API economy, is most efficiently achieved, in the long run, on decentralized platforms. Negotiations made on a level playing field are fairer, resolve quicker, and encourage more business.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Future of Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782201
scope_conditions: in the long run

subjectOf.text: Because we are reared in a centralized world we reflexively turn to centralized solutions, but a decentralized approach is more effective for global problems, since decentralized networks encourage interoperability through bureaucratic transparency and thereby integrate data better than a single dictating source.
subjectOf.abstract: Reared in a centralized world, we reflexively turn to centralized solutions. But a decentralized approach is more effective for such global problems. Decentralized networks encourage interoperability through bureaucratic transparency.
subjectOf.citation: Craig Calcaterra, Wulf A. Kaal, Future of Decentralization (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3782201
scope_conditions: global crises demanding coordination of many people's information

subjectOf.text: The ethos of interoperability in software development arose from a survival calculation rather than altruism: developers recognized that software which could not work across platforms would not survive.
subjectOf.abstract: In turn, the realization in the software development community that interoperability of software means survivability, gave rise to an ethos of interoperability.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization – Why We Need Technology Infrastructure Upgrades (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808859
scope_conditions: software development community, especially in its early period

subjectOf.text: APIs dissolve traditional value-chain hierarchies because a company can obtain features more cheaply and more easily by connecting separate products through APIs than by controlling the entire value chain itself.
subjectOf.abstract: Through the use of APIs, companies no longer need to control the entire value chain because it is much cheaper and technologically often easier to create application features in separate products that connect via APIs to existing ecosystems and/or other products.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization – Why We Need Technology Infrastructure Upgrades (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808859

subjectOf.text: Cloud computing increased connectivity but simultaneously produced monolithic, siloed applications built for a single business, department, or role, and that fragmentation of data and content now impairs collaboration as well as the search, organization, and discovery of content.
subjectOf.abstract: Cloud computing has significantly increased connectivity in society and business but at the same time contributed to the creation of monolithic applications that solve a very specific problem for a specific business / department / role.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization – Why We Need Technology Infrastructure Upgrades (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808859

subjectOf.text: Cloud computing is the enabling substrate for decentralized solutions rather than their competitor, because it has already established that applications can talk to each other, an integration that decentralized networks will extend.
subjectOf.abstract: Cloud computing enables future decentralized solutions because it already allows applications to talk to each other.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization – Why We Need Technology Infrastructure Upgrades (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808859
scope_conditions: requires applications to integrate regardless of technological and physical environment

subjectOf.text: Decentralized technology systems require interoperability for survivability, yet most platforms attempt to go it alone in an effort to become the next Bitcoin, so decentralized community silos proliferate and the required infrastructure, which no single protocol can build, does not get built.
subjectOf.abstract: Decentralized technology systems require interoperability for survivability. Yet, most platforms attempt to make it alone in an effort to become the next Bitcoin. As a result, decentralized community silos proliferate.
subjectOf.citation: Wulf A. Kaal, Decentralization Neutralizers (2021). SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=3808873
scope_conditions: decentralized protocol ecosystems in the early 2020s

subjectOf.text: A unified governance framework is hard to establish in the federated model because each participating entity maintains its own AI systems and datasets, producing variation in standards, protocols, and formats.
subjectOf.abstract: In a federated AI model, different entities or organizations maintain their own AI systems and datasets. This can lead to variations in standards, protocols, and formats used, making it difficult to establish a unified governance framework.
